ITC: Building a Future-Forward Enterprise 
for a Viksit Bharat
ITC has always lived by its vision of creating larger value for all stakeholders while contributing meaningfully to national 
priorities. Guided by its credo Nation First: Sab Saath Badhein, the Company has built world-class Indian brands, 
strengthened domestic value chains, invested in advanced manufacturing, deepened farmer partnerships, and accelerated 
digital, AI-led and R&D-driven innovation. As India advances towards a Viksit Bharat, ITC continues to shape a future-ready 
enterprise anchored in competitiveness, sustainability, and inclusive growth. Its large-scale initiatives to conserve and 
replenish natural resources, together with impactful climate action and social programmes, are helping build a more resilient, 
inclusive, and future-ready India. Reinforcing this commitment, the Company has redefined its Mission, Vision and Values to 
inspire greater purpose-led action and an even deeper contribution to national progress.

strengthen competitiveness, profitability, and resilience. Despite the challenging environment, it continues to unlock

investments, while advancing ITC’s commitment to a climate-resilient and inclusive future. Enterprise levers 
strengthened by digital and sustainability are lending unique sources of competitiveness for future readiness.

ITC has invested in building world-class national manufacturing assets across FMCG, Paperboards, Packaging, and 
export-oriented value-added Agri products. Its ecosystem of over 250 factories and partnerships with more than 7,500 MSMEs 
enables ITC to produce high-quality products, boost exports, substitute imports, promote local entrepreneurship, and support 
inclusive value chains that empower farmers and communities. In the true spirit of ‘Make in India’, nearly 90% of ITC’s value 
addition takes place within the country. Recognising the growth opportunities in the Indian consumer market, ITC has made 
substantial investments in establishing 12 state-of-the-art Integrated Consumer Goods Manufacturing and Logistics (ICML) 
facilities, including food factories, across India. These facilities, which are today proximally located to major demand centres, 
have emerged as vibrant hubs of innovation, technology, sustainability, and diversity.

New Vector – ITCMAARS
ITCMAARS (Metamarket for Advanced Agriculture and Rural Services) is a phygital agri ecosystem that integrates digital 
tech with on-ground engagement, with Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) as the pivot to enable farmer 
empowerment. Building on the e-Choupal ecosystem, ITCMAARS provides hyper-local solutions, including personalised 
advisories, weather insights, input access, credit, and market linkages. By enabling data-led decision-making and 
demand-responsive value chains, ITCMAARS helps enhance productivity, resilience,  and farmer incomes at scale.

ITC: Building a Future-Forward Enterprise for a Viksit Bharat
Climate Risk Assessment
Climate Action Initiatives
ITC’s climate action, anchored in its Sustainability 2.0 agenda, combines climate risk assessment, decarbonisation, 
adaptation, ecosystem restoration and circularity. ITC has set a target of achieving Net Zero Operations by 2050, while 
actively reducing GHG intensity and scaling green infrastructure, including renewable energy. Climate-smart agriculture, 
social and farm forestry, and water stewardship programmes build climate resilience and adaptive capacity across 
value chains.
ITC has used different purpose-specific AI tools for carrying out climate risk 
assessments at 140 sites for rainfall, flood, heat, drought and wind, as well as 
detailed farm-level studies on its agri value chains. Based on the assessments, 
it has undertaken targeted site-specific interventions to climate-proof its 
physical infrastructure, build resilience in agriculture and support climate 
adaptation. This has helped ITC integrate climate science, advanced technologies 
and data-driven insights into its sustainability strategy.

Your Directors
S. Puri
Sanjiv Puri (63), DIN: 00280529, is the Chairman & 
Managing Director of ITC Limited.
Puri was appointed as a Wholetime Director on the  
Board of ITC with effect from December 6, 2015,  
Chief Executive Ofﬁcer in February 2017 and  
re-designated as the Managing Director in May 2018.  
He was appointed as the Chairman effective May 13, 2019. 
He is an alumnus of IIT Kanpur and Wharton School  
of Business, USA.
Puri joined ITC in January 1986. During his career of

THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
The practice of Corporate Governance in ITC takes place 
at three interlinked levels:
Strategic supervision by the Board of Directors
Strategic management by the Corporate Management 
Committee 
Executive management by the Divisional Chief Executive 
assisted by the Divisional 
Management Committee
The three-tier governance structure ensures that:
(a)  Strategic supervision (on behalf of Shareholders), being 
free from involvement in the task of strategic management  
of the Company, can be conducted with objectivity,  
thereby sharpening accountability of management;
(b)  Strategic management of the Company, uncluttered 
by the day-to-day tasks of executive management, 
remains focused and energised; and
(c)  Executive management of the divisional business, free  
from collective strategic responsibilities for ITC as 
a whole, remains focused on enhancing the quality, 
efﬁciency and effectiveness of the business to achieve 
best-in-class performance. 
The core roles of the key entities ﬂow from this structure.

of each entity. In order to discharge such responsibiliti
